notes: The parts list matched an 'Arduino board' to arduino-uno, but the circuit image shows a Raspberry Pi GPIO header (labelled GND, GP17, etc.). The image is the authority, so I used a new raspberry-pi part type instead of arduino-uno.
Pi ports are named by function plus physical pin number for the repeated ones (e.g. GND.9 is physical pin 9).
The black wire runs from Pi GND (pin 9) to breadboard row 15. The purple wire runs from GPIO17 (pin 11) to breadboard row 18.
The buzzer body hides the holes it plugs into. I assumed its legs are in column e of rows 15 and 18, in the same strips as the wire ends in column a.
Buzzer polarity: port 1 is taken as positive and goes to GPIO17. Port 2 is negative and goes to GND.
The wire ends at the Pi header are pushed onto the header pins. The catalogue only has jumper-wire (not male-to-female), so jumper-wire is used.
